chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The child lives for six months, and for seven months, and for nine months, but does not live for eight months.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the viability of a fetus born after eight months of gestation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi records Imam Ali’s (AS) statement that a fetus born after six, seven, or nine months is viable, while one born after eight months is not. This specific exclusion of the eighth month reflects the classical medical understanding prevalent in early Islamic times, which viewed the eighth month as a period of fragility where survival was uncertain, a view later nuanced by scholars who distinguished between 'viability' and 'certainty of life'.
